From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

ses (“six”) +‎ -o

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈseso/
  • Rhymes: -eso
  • Syllabification: se‧so

Noun

[edit]

seso (accusative singular seson, plural sesoj, accusative plural sesojn)

  1. sixsome (group of six)
    Synonym: sesopo
  2. the digit or figure six

See also

[edit]
Playing cards in Esperanto · ludkartoj (layout · text)
aso duo trio kvaro kvino seso sepo
oko naŭo deko fanto, bubo damo reĝo ĵokero

Further reading

[edit]
  • “seso”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “seso”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-present

seso

  1. nominative singular masculine of sesa (“remaining”)

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin sēnsus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈseso/ [ˈse.so]
  • Rhymes: -eso
  • Syllabification: se‧so

Noun

[edit]

seso m (plural sesos)

  1. brain
    Synonym: cerebro
    volarle los sesos ― to blow someone's brains out
  2. (often in plural) brainwork, brain power

Derived terms

[edit]
  • calentarse los sesos
  • devanarse los sesos
  • la cabeza blanca y el seso por venir
  • sesera
  • seso vegetal
  • volarse los sesos (“to blow one's brains out”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “seso”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
